newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bond prices rise but market haunted by EMU.
newsitem.headline: Danish bond prices rise but market haunted by EMU.

text.p: Danish bond prices edged up on Wednesday on a market still nervous of possible changes to the EMU timetable, even though Denmark has already opted out of Economic and Monetary Union.
"The problem is that there are not many buyers in this uncertain and volatile market," a dealer said.

At 1220 GMT the benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was up 0.07 point from Tuesday's close, to 108.54 in turnover of over four billion crowns, while its March future -- expiring on Friday -- was untraded at 110.65. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 lost 0.21 point to 86.69.
The crown traded at 3.8170 per mark, continuing to firm from Tuesday's 3.8200.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany widened to 82 basis points from 81 earlier. --Stig Pedersen, Copenhagen newsroom, 45-33-969650
